newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY MILLING WHEAT, BARLEY UP, FEED WHEAT DOWN.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY MILLING WHEAT, BARLEY UP, FEED WHEAT DOWN.

text.p: Lack of supply drove milling wheat and barley prices limit-up on the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) while feed wheat went limit-down, traders said on Thursday.

Total grains futures turnover on the BCE was steady in volume terms at 1,240 lots compared with 1,256 on Wednesday, but fell in forints terms to 487.4 million forints, compared with 577.9 million on Wednesday.
The change was due to the fact that relatively cheap feed wheat, which usually trades in low volume, accounted for three quarters of daily turnover with 855 lots.

"It is highly unusual for feed wheat to have higher volume turnover than milling wheat," said Janos Szolyka of Swap brokerage. He added that both the supply and the buying side was strong for feed wheat.
"Producers want to sell their crop...and traders think current price levels would allow for (profitable) export, if exports start at all."

Feed wheat prices rose the daily allowed 400 forints per tonne for all but the September maturity, which rose 230 forints to 17,500. October finished at 17,600 forints, December at 18,100 and May at 21,000.
October, December and March feed wheat will have the limit restriction lifted on Friday as those maturities went limit-down for three days. However, Szolyka did not expect the trend to continue.
"Feed wheat prices would probably have stabilised in a day or two anyway," he said.
The milling wheat price rise was again only restricted by the daily limit as fears of scarce supply prevailed.
"Very little of this year's wheat crop is up to (high) BCE standards," Szolyka said.
"While a lot of wheat is actually good enough for the mills to buy it, it does not meet BCE standards".
Persistent rains have lowered the gluten content of this year's wheat crop while germination is considerably above usual levels.
Milling wheat prices finished at between 27,300 forints for September 1997 and 27,800 for October 1998 in moderate turnover.
Euro wheat prices went limit-up for all maturities in sympathy with milling wheat prices.
However, Szolyka said that next year euro wheat was likely to be more popular than milling wheat.
Euro wheat, which started trading last Friday, was introduced only for maturities from August 1998, in order not to interfere with other wheat prices.
Euro wheat will also be freed on Friday for August and September.
Feed barley prices went limit-up for all but the December contract on closing of speculative positions, Szolyka said.
Maize remained in the shadow and only registered significant turnover in the December maturity which dropped 130 forints to 18,600.
(Lot size=20,000 kgs $=200.36 Hungarian forints)
-- Denes Albert, Budapest newsroom +36 1 327 4040
